11.label: Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's
11.desc: Glass everywhere at Rafe Claesz's. Someone went through the shop window, with a cobble at the dead of the night, took whatever was in the till, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing a cart with the tail-board up. (Patricians' Hill)

14.label: Magdalena Kempe
14.desc: Magdalena Kempe, the owner's partner in trade. Has ink-black fingers; works a printer's press. (Accused in: Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's)

25.label: Beadle Bakker
25.desc: A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked. Slot them into a verb to help. Thorough: Finds one more thing at every scene.

29.label: Barbel Bader
29.desc: Barbel Bader, a journeyman turned off. Owes a great deal to a moneylender in the Stews. (Accused in: Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's)

43.label: Bess Fletcher
43.desc: Bess Fletcher, a receiver from the Market. Wears civet and rosewater, like a courtier. (Accused in: Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's)

68.desc: The bands have sworn to one shell now, and the shell has a king: Stoffel Ebner, the King of Thunes, on a barrel in a cellar under the Warrens. The Vendetta surges every week. Go in Disguise: with the ledger, to break it; with Wit, to parley; with Instinct and Coin, to be tried by its court and stay.

71.label: Protection in the Night Market
71.desc: Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Bartel Welser's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk. (The Warrens)

77.label: A Torn Tally
77.desc: Half a tally-stick from the Tanner Lane Lodging-house. Somebody spends their evenings there, and owes.

78.label: A Hobnail Scar
78.desc: A deep gouge at the foot of the door, the kind a hobnailed boot makes. A big boot, and a kick.

79.label: Stoffel Ebner
79.desc: Stoffel Ebner, a bravo of the Stews. Wears great hobnailed boots, a soldier's. (Accused in: Protection in the Night Market)

83.label: Unanswered: Burglary at Dyer the Goldsmith's
83.desc: The trail went cold. Anneke Kessler walked. With the Rolls, this can be opened again in Study.

84.label: Rumour from Rattle
84.desc: Rattle heard something about Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's: "They smelled like a gentleman. Civet, or some such."

85.label: The Slashed Awning
85.desc: Cut from the street, an hour before the gate bell, when the lane is still busy. They wanted to be seen.

87.label: Dirck Hobson
87.desc: Dirck Hobson, a sergeant of the Watch. Plays at dice every night in a cellar in the Stews. (Accused in: Protection in the Night Market)

89.label: Hue and Cry: Anneke Kessler
89.desc: Anneke Kessler has been seen again. They walked once. The trail is warm, for now. (The Harbour)

94.label: A Left-Handed Stroke
94.desc: Whoever did this stood on the right and worked with their left hand. The angle is plain to anyone who has seen a butcher.

95.label: Anneke Kessler
95.desc: Anneke Kessler, the fugitive. Left-handed. Writes with a hooked wrist. (Accused in: Hue and Cry: Anneke Kessler)

100.label: Protection in the Night Market
100.desc: Stallholders have been paying for "protection" for months. Now Hal Kürschner's stall has had its awning slashed and its stock in the gutter for refusing. Nobody else will talk. (The Market)

110.label: Lienhard Stromer
110.desc: Lienhard Stromer, a bravo of the Stews. Drives a dray with a lame grey mule. (Accused in: Protection in the Night Market)

116.label: The Slashed Awning
116.desc: Cut from the street, an hour before the gate bell, when the lane is still busy. They wanted to be seen.

130.label: Band: The Velvet Knives
130.desc: Sworn together by Anneke Kessler, Sworn A0, Sworn A1, who all walked from you. They feed the Vendetta every week. Go in Disguise to build a case against them.

journal.text: Sworn A2, Sworn B0, Sworn B1: every one of them walked away from one of your cases. Now they drink in the same cellar, and call themselves the Velvet Knives.

journal.title: Week 11
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. Out there, the people who walked are talking about you. The broadsheet-sellers count the thieves abroad, and sing the number in the Market. Anselm Vogt spoiled a token of yours. The ledger: no case closed; 4 open; 15 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Wounded

journal.title: A Long Rest
journal.text: A week of nothing. Long walks outside the walls. Small beer and bread. Your hands stop shaking on the fourth day. On the seventh you want to go back to the Watch-house, which is either a good sign or a very bad one.

journal.title: The Rival Takes a Case
journal.text: Anselm Vogt is working Burglary at Dyer the Goldsmith's from the other side, with the Provost's watchmen. Answer it first, or they will.

journal.title: The Coquille
journal.text: You have seen the same advocate at every hearing, the same faces at every cellar door. Behind the city's crime there is a court, a barrel for a throne, and a king. They call it the Coquille. Go in Disguise to get at its books.

journal.title: A Word

journal.title: Back at the Scene

journal.title: Nothing Came of It
journal.text: Rattle notices you did nothing with what they told you. They will be slower to tell you again.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Fever
journal.text: You stand in the Market outside the Watch-house for an hour and cannot make yourself go in. Your hands will not stop shaking. You need rest, and soon.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: The night-watchman keeps his hours in his head. Two, quiet. Three, the shutter open. Somebody knew the house, and somebody was in and out between the bells. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: Week 5
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The Provost has sent an examiner of his own. The ledger: no case closed; 2 open; 8 Coin in hand.

journal.title: The Provost's Examiner
journal.text: Anselm Vogt has the Provost's letter and a desk on the other side of the Market. They will work your cases from the other side: close them first, spoil your scenes, pay your witnesses to forget. Question them, buy them, frighten them, or shadow them; find their weakness twice and the Council sends them home.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Dyer the Goldsmith's

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: You go back over Kramer the Goldsmith's. You find: The Getaway. A neighbour, leaning on the gate, offers a name: Barbel Bader. The back room stayed locked, and whatever it held stays there.

journal.title: A Warning
journal.text: "Burglary," says Rattle, "in Patricians' Hill. Soon. Don't ask me how I know."

journal.title: A Round Walked
journal.text: Lienhard Bakker walks the round without complaint. The Council's ledger reads your name.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Sworn In
journal.text: Lienhard Bakker takes the oath at the Watch-house door. A parish beadle with a staff and a loud voice. Knocks on doors without complaining and whips beggars without being asked.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Week 2
journal.text: Lodging and dues take 1. The Council's stipend: 1 Coin. The ledger: no case closed; 1 open; 5 Coin in hand.

journal.title: Back at the Scene
journal.text: The night-watchman keeps his hours in his head. Two, quiet. Three, the shutter open. Somebody knew the house, and somebody was in and out between the bells. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Round
journal.text: Two drunks, a stolen goose and a lost dog. The dog was the most reasonable of them. Your feet ache all the way up to your skull.

journal.title: Sleep
journal.text: You sleep from vespers to terce and wake up hungry. The world is still there. So are you.

journal.title: Partial Results
journal.text: Without a Physician's Case, you only get part of it. The blade was a chisel, chipped at one corner. Find the chisel, find the burglar. You worked into the dark, and it cost you.

journal.title: A Word from Rattle
journal.text: A folded paper pushed under the Watch-house door, about Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's. Rattle does not sign things.

journal.title: At the Scene
journal.text: You go in past the beadle at Kramer the Goldsmith's. The back shutter has been forced with something flat and patient, and the strongbox stands open like a mouth. You come away with The Pried Shutter, The Inventory. A name for the board: Magdalena Kempe. The back room stayed locked, and the hard way in wore you out.

journal.title: The Carolina
journal.text: They gave you the Emperor's law with the letter: two witnesses, or a confession, or nothing. You have read it. You know exactly which pages you will tear out, and in what order. First, the burglary on the desk.

journal.title: New Case: Burglary at Kramer the Goldsmith's
journal.text: Glass everywhere at Rafe Claesz's. Someone went through the shop window, with a cobble at the dead of the night, took whatever was in the till, and was gone before the watchman finished shouting. A neighbour reports seeing a cart with the tail-board up.

f129.name: the de Groot Workshop by the Close
